sections.heading: Welcome back
points: School is back for another year after an 11-week summer — one week longer than usual
Summer-camp friends did something different every day
A newsletter comes at the start of each month through May; the last one covers May and June together
It goes out on the 1st, or the 2nd or 3rd when the 1st falls on a weekend
Read the announcements, reminders and monthly calendar so nothing is missed

sections.heading: Snack calendar
points: Every family signs up for a turn on the snack calendar
Sign up once a month to keep things fair
Booking months ahead? Note it in your own calendar a day or two before — parents do forget
September to December are open; days off are already taken out
Half days still need a morning snack — everyone leaves by 11:30
See the snack and allergy email for what to bring

sections.heading: Blue bags and nap bags
points: Bring your child’s blue bag, and nap bag if needed, on Mondays
Blue bags go home every other Friday, not every week — return them the following Monday
Nap bags go home every Friday, unless your child missed that day
Keep napping items out of the blue bag; the two are stored apart

sections.heading: Pickup times
points: Pickup times are strict
Late pickups are charged a late fee

sections.heading: Car line
points: Bring a paper sign with your child’s first name, large enough to read from a distance
If the teacher is squinting into the afternoon glare, hold the sign out the window
Dismissal starts at 3:00 and is done by 3:05, in two lines side by side
Pull up at least to the next set of stairs before getting out to buckle your child — it keeps the line moving

sections.heading: Show and Tell
points: Every Wednesday, in every classroom
Bring something your child made — a drawing, a story, a Lego build, a book
Store-bought toys don’t help, and stay home anyway
It’s optional — don’t push a child who isn’t ready; most join in after a month or two
A child can sit with the group and watch without presenting

sections.heading: Birthdays
points: No goodie bags for the class
Donate a book instead — the school writes your child’s name and birthday inside
The teacher or office will get in touch with details as the date nears
Email the office about a week ahead so it doesn’t clash with another birthday or school event

sections.heading: This month
points: No extra days off in September after Labor Day
September is for settling in: new students learn the routine, returning students pick it back up, and classroom cultures take shape
Consistent attendance now pays off all year
Aim to arrive before 8:30 — drop-offs get easier as the year goes on

sections.heading: Questions
points: Call the office at (781) 526-5368
